title: Signal stitching: dashboard playlist & trace primer
content:
Purpose
This is a short, operational-first plan for stitching signals across the inference stack (API -> router -> runtime -> model). Focus is on: concise metric definitions, a minimal trace-span naming convention, and a small set of dashboard "mini-lenses" operators can use to jump from symptom -> hypothesis -> action.

Context and motivation
- We have many dashboard panels and overlapping metrics across teams; investigation time is high because signals are siloed.
- Goal: reduce mean-time-to-hypothesis by making a deterministic path from a top-level symptom (eg: 95th latency increase) to the relevant traces and low-level KPIs.
- This doc proposes: (1) a compact metric contract, (2) trace span naming + key attributes, (3) three dashboard lenses and their drillflows, and (4) a short migration checklist.

1) Compact metric contract (minimal set intended for rollout)
- request.count: counter per route/model/version; cardinality: route, model, model_version, region, tenant_id
- request.latency_ms: histogram (p50/p90/p95/p99); cardinality: route, model, model_version, region, tenant_id, span_phase
- kvcache.hit_rate: gauge (0..1) per model/model_variant/region; cardinality: model, model_variant, region, tenant_id
- batch.size: histogram for batching pipeline; cardinality: route, model, instance_type
- token.per_request: gauge average tokens emitted; cardinality: route, model
- fallback.count: counter when request routed to fallback variant; cardinality: route, fallback_reason, source_region
- error.rate: counter with labels (error_class, http_status, model); cardinality: full but prefer coarse error_class values (Timeout, OOM, InvalidInput, ModelError)

Notes on cardinality and costs:
- Keep tenant_id in primary ingestion only when sampling or for high-value tenants. For public panels use tenant-bucket (low/med/high) to avoid cardinal explosion.
- Use derived signals for aggressive rollouts (eg: route+model p95 vs baseline p95).

2) Trace span naming and attributes (proposal)
- High-level convention: <layer>.<operation> (eg: api.parse, router.route-decision, runtime.kv-lookup, runtime.decode).
- Required attributes on root span: request_id, route, model, model_version, tenant_bucket, region, priority_tier
- Important attributes on intermediate spans:
  - router.route-decision: route_candidates (count), selected_variant, fallback_taken (bool), selection_latency_ms
  - runtime.kv-lookup: kvcache_hit (bool), key_hash_prefix, lookup_latency_ms
  - runtime.compile-or-load: compile_ms, bytes_loaded, quantization_mode
  - runtime.generate: tokens_generated, decode_ms, batching_size
- Sampling guidance: sample all traces where error.rate > threshold OR where latency.p95 > historical + 20% for last hour. For bursts sample ratio increases; keep 5% baseline for general traffic.

3) Dashboard "mini-lenses" and drillflows
Lens A — Latency Surface (operational starter)
- Top panels: request.latency_ms (p50/p90/p95/p99) by route and model; request.count; batch.size distribution
- Investigation steps:
  1) If p95 spike: toggle to per-region and per-model_version; check fallback.count and router.selection_latency_ms
  2) If spike correlated with batch.size change: inspect batch.size histogram and instance_type saturation; check CPU/GPU util panels (linked infra dashboard)
  3) If kvcache.hit_rate drops: open trace samples where runtime.kv-lookup.kvcache_hit=false and inspect prefix provenance
- Useful quick queries: top 10 routes by p95 delta, top tenants by p95 deviation, recent canary deploys (link to rollout log)

Lens B — Correctness/Quality Signal (ops + product)
- Top panels: error.rate by error_class, fallback.count by reason, token.per_request median vs expected
- Investigation steps:
  1) If fallback.count rises: check router.route-decision.selected_variant and fallback_reason, then trace selected traces to see whether selected_variant returned early (timeout)
  2) If error.rate increases with unchanged traffic: inspect model_version rollout timestamps and linked GitHub PRs (linked_artifacts)

Lens C — Cost & Throughput (capacity ops)
- Top panels: request.count, tokens emitted (estimated cost), batch.size, instance GPU utilization, KV cache eviction rate
- Investigation: sudden cost increase -> check tokens per request and fallback count (fallbacks to larger models blow up token counts); check autoscaler events and spike timing

4) Dashboards: UX suggestions
- Buttons on top of each lens: "Jump to traces" (pre-filled service/route/model filters), "Open recent deploys" (links to rollout console), "Open suspect traces" (top slow traces in last 15m).
- Panels should link to an investigation notebook template (observability template) for faster RCA handoff.
- Small, actionable panels only. Replace dense tables with top-10 lists + sparklines.

5) Migration checklist (practical steps to replace old metrics)
- Inventory current panels and tag ones we will retire (owner + panel id).
- Implement metric exporters for any missing labels (start with request.latency_ms and kvcache.hit_rate).
- Backfill heuristics: for 90-day baseline compute p95 baseline for each route/model_version; store baseline summary in config store to power anomaly rules.
- Rollout plan:
  - Week 0: instrument + QA (low traffic region), enable dashboards in read-only mode
  - Week 1: sample alerts, invite SRE + runtime oncall to review
  - Week 2: flip panels for primary ops, mark old panels deprecated

Open questions / unresolved items
- Should tenant_id be included in request.latency ingestion for all customers or only enterprise? (cost vs signal fidelity tradeoff)
- What sampling rate for traces for low-volume routes gives good MTTI without cost blowup? Current proposal: baseline 5%, escalate to 50% on anomalies.
- How to represent multi-model fanout traces concisely? (proposal: parent trace with child spans annotated with model_variant)

Next steps and owners
- Instrumentation tasks: runtime team to add kvcache.hit_rate and batch.size histograms (owner: Marco)
- Trace attributes: SDK change to add root labels (owner: Jin)
- Dashboards: build three lens dashboards and the "Jump to traces" links (owner: Aisha)
- SRE review: schedule tabletop for migration (owner: Priya)

Notes to self
- Keep this doc short; move deep examples into an "examples" notebook (CONFLUENCE-OBS-EXAMPLES).
- When we add redo/rollout links, include a brief privacy review for tenant_id usage.

References
- Existing observability inventory (link in linked_artifacts)
- Quick trace naming cheatsheet: keep layer.operation stable across releases to avoid search fragmentation.

End of draft
